correctness.rationale: A reversible nonnegative matrix is self-adjoint in the population-weighted inner product. The exact constant-on-rate-class compression depends only on total cross-class flux t, which is at most min(Pa,Qb). Its two-dimensional symmetric matrix is diag(a,b) minus a positive semidefinite rank-one matrix times t; the top eigenvalue strictly decreases for distinct a,b. A concrete full-cross-class positive witness attains the bound and is irreducible. Equality in the Rayleigh principle forces uniform cross-class row sums in each class; conversely those sums lift a strictly positive Perron eigenvector. Boundary a=b follows from constant row totals. Exact rational example and 420 finite spectral comparisons passed with the bundled program. These checks are supplemental, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Theorem 3.6 of arXiv:2602.23885v2 gives sharp two-type results; its Section 8.1 provides a general k-type SDP and therefore implicitly covers the optimization numerically. The new claim is the explicit all-k two-rate evaluation without assumed lumpability together with an if-and-only-if characterization of every optimizer. These analytical statements were not located in materially inspected main source sections or retrieved closely related material. General spectral variational tools are prior art. Historical priority remains uncertain because an existing block-compression theorem could imply this result.
residual_risks: The motivating paper general SDP implicitly solves each finite instance; novelty is solely the closed-form two-rate evaluation and necessity/sufficiency classification of all minimizers.
General matrix spectral optimization and equitable-partition theorems elsewhere may directly imply this classwise rigidity.
Supporting social-contact and equitable-partition references were inspected at abstract level only and cannot be used to rule out entire-document coverage.
The theorem allows diagonal entries; it does not apply directly to loopless or forced sparse contact networks.

value.rationale: Two distinct total contact rates with arbitrary fine subgroups form a motivated data-resolution regime in contact surveys. A complete arbitrary-dimension exact optimization with a two-dimensional closed formula and a necessary-and-sufficient description of all attaining matrices replaces generic multivariate numerical SDP within this regime. This also yields a sharp criterion for the existence of a subcritical reciprocal epidemic network, exhibited by a four-type exact witness with one group rate above one. No claim about epidemic final size or empirical effectiveness is inferred.
